title: X OAuth 2.0 refresh_token placeholders and non-value fields
summary: A refresh_token field holding an angle placeholder, a template or shell reference, a masked or empty value, a prose mention, and a token response with only the type, lifetime and scope members.
rationale: A placeholder, reference, masked or empty value carries no credential, and the field name in prose is an everyday term. The token type word, the expires_in number and the scope list are public members of the same exchange and are not values of the refresh token.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: these inputs hold no credential value. That a placeholder, reference, masked or empty value, prose mention or public identifier is not a value is a project decision, not a X statement.

sources.supports: A refresh token allows an application to obtain a new access token without prompting the user. ... In addition, you will also need to pass in your refresh_token, set your grant_type to be a refresh_token, and define your client_id.

Success response (HTTP 200): {"token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 7200, "access_token": "...", "refresh_token": "...", "scope": "..."}. Store the refresh_token (and current access_token) against the user

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
